To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mutational spectra of p53 gene in different types of human cancer have a tissue-specific pattern, and that the mutational "hot spots" distribution in 5–8 exons of p53 gene is determined by the specificity of cell divisions conditions in vivo and cell culture in vitro.
the mutational spectra of p53 in different tumors are not the same, and that the differences are due to the different cell types in which the tumor develops.
the mutational spectrum of the p53 tumor suppressor gene in human cancers is tissue-specific and depends on the type of cell division in vivo and in culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the mechanisms of the formation of the mutational spectra of tumor suppressor gene p53 in the germline and tumors, the role of mutagenesis in tumorogenesis, the role of the environment and the genetic factors in the development of cancer.
the study of mutational spectra of tumor suppressor gene p53 in germline and somatic mutations.

the comparative analysis of mutational spectra of p53 in different tumors, obtained in vivo and in cell culture in vitro, with the purpose to reveal the role of cell division conditions and other factors in the formation of mutational spectra in gene p53.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutational spectrum of gene p53 reflects the mutational processes in the cells of the human body, which are controlled by the environment.
the mutational hot spots are a consequence of mutagenic action of the endogenous mutagens.
mutational spectra of p53 gene in tumors and cell lines is a reflection of mutational processes in the genome of the organism and the conditions of the cell division in vivo and in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "hot spots" are the sites of gene p53, where the DNA repair mechanisms are less effective.
the hot spots of p53 gene mutations are not a constant, but rather dynamic, and their distribution is determined by the conditions of the cell division.
the distribution of "hot spots", which are characteristic for germline mutations, is determined by cell division conditions in vitro and in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mutational spectra of tumor p53 are different for tumors of different cell origin and for different cell lines.
the mutational spectra of the p53 gene is tissue specific.
the mutational spectra of the p53 gene are not identical between different types of tumors, and the mutational hot spots in the p53 gene can be used as markers of tumor histogenesis.
